nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $\lambda$ a real number and $a_1, \dots, a_n$ natural numbers. If $(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is a strict underapproximation of $\lambda$, then $a_i \ge 2$ for every $1 \le i \le n$.
nodes.title: Denominators of a strict underapproximation are at least two

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $\lambda$ a real number and $a_1, \dots, a_n$ natural numbers. If $(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is a nondecreasing underapproximation of $\lambda$, then $a_i \ge 2$ for every $1 \le i \le n$.
nodes.title: Denominators of a nondecreasing underapproximation are at least two

nodes.summary: If $a = (a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is a nondecreasing underapproximation of a real number $\lambda$, then $a$ lies in $\mathcal{E}_n^{\le}$, that is, $2 \le a_1 \le \dots \le a_n$.
nodes.title: Nondecreasing underapproximations have Egyptian denominator tuples

nodes.summary: A tuple $(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ of natural numbers lies in $\mathcal{E}_n^{\le}$ when $2 \le a_1 \le a_2 \le \dots \le a_n$, that is, every $a_i$ is at least $2$ and the tuple is nondecreasing.
nodes.title: Nondecreasing Egyptian denominator tuples

nodes.summary: Let $\lambda$ be a real number and $a = (a_1, \dots, a_n)$ a tuple of natural numbers. Then $a$ is a nondecreasing underapproximation of $\lambda$ when $n \ge 1$, $\lambda > 0$, $a$ lies in $\mathcal{E}_n^{\le}$ (that is, $2 \le a_1 \le \dots \le a_n$), and $\sum_{i=1}^{n} 1/a_i < \lambda$, the sum taken in the real numbers.
nodes.title: Egyptian underapproximations with nondecreasing denominators

nodes.summary: If $a = (a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is a strict underapproximation of a real number $\lambda$, then $a$ lies in $\mathcal{E}_n^{<}$, that is, $2 \le a_1 < \dots < a_n$.
nodes.title: Strict underapproximations have strictly increasing Egyptian denominators

nodes.summary: A tuple $(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ of natural numbers lies in $\mathcal{E}_n^{<}$ when $2 \le a_1 < a_2 < \dots < a_n$, that is, every $a_i$ is at least $2$ and the tuple is strictly increasing.
nodes.title: Strictly increasing Egyptian denominator tuples

nodes.summary: Let $\lambda$ be a real number and $a = (a_1, \dots, a_n)$ a tuple of natural numbers. Then $a$ is a strict underapproximation of $\lambda$ when $n \ge 1$, $\lambda > 0$, $a$ lies in $\mathcal{E}_n^{<}$ (that is, $2 \le a_1 < \dots < a_n$, so the unit fractions are distinct), and $\sum_{i=1}^{n} 1/a_i < \lambda$, the sum taken in the real numbers.
nodes.title: Egyptian underapproximations with strictly increasing denominators

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $\lambda$ a real number and $a_1, \dots, a_n$ natural numbers. If $(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is a nondecreasing underapproximation of $\lambda$, then $a_i \le a_j$ whenever $1 \le i \le j \le n$.
nodes.title: Denominators of a nondecreasing underapproximation are nondecreasing

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $\lambda$ a real number and $a_1, \dots, a_n$ natural numbers. If $(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is a strict underapproximation of $\lambda$, then $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Strict underapproximations have at least one term

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $\lambda$ a real number and $a_1, \dots, a_n$ natural numbers. If $(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is a nondecreasing underapproximation of $\lambda$, then $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Nondecreasing underapproximations have at least one term

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $\lambda$ a real number and $a_1, \dots, a_n$ natural numbers. If $(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is a strict underapproximation of $\lambda$, then $a_i < a_j$ whenever $1 \le i < j \le n$.
nodes.title: Denominators of a strict underapproximation increase strictly

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $\lambda$ a real number and $a_1, \dots, a_n$ natural numbers. If $(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is a strict underapproximation of $\lambda$, then $\sum_{i=1}^{n} 1/a_i < \lambda$, the sum taken in the real numbers.
nodes.title: A strict underapproximation stays below its target

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $\lambda$ a real number and $a_1, \dots, a_n$ natural numbers. If $(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is a nondecreasing underapproximation of $\lambda$, then $\sum_{i=1}^{n} 1/a_i < \lambda$.
nodes.title: A nondecreasing underapproximation stays below its target

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $\lambda$ a real number and $a_1, \dots, a_n$ natural numbers. If $(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is a strict underapproximation of $\lambda$, then $\lambda > 0$.
nodes.title: The target of a strict underapproximation is positive

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $\lambda$ a real number and $a_1, \dots, a_n$ natural numbers. If $(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is a nondecreasing underapproximation of $\lambda$, then $\lambda > 0$.
nodes.title: The target of a nondecreasing underapproximation is positive

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $\lambda$ a real number and $a_1, \dots, a_n$ natural numbers. If $(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is a strict underapproximation of $\lambda$, then it is also a nondecreasing underapproximation of $\lambda$.
nodes.title: Strict underapproximations are nondecreasing underapproximations

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
